references.text: Repeats the commandment about the Passover lamb from Numbers, including the prohibition against breaking any of its bones.
David's psalm about the righteous one, stating that the Lord preserves all his bones; not one of them shall be broken. Seen as a prophetic reference to the Messiah.
The soldiers did not break Jesus' legs because he was already dead, unlike the two others who were crucified with him.
John quotes directly that 'not a bone shall be broken on him,' showing that Jesus is the true Passover lamb who fulfills this prophecy.
Paul identifies Christ as our Passover lamb who has been sacrificed, linking Jesus' sacrifice to the regulations for the Passover lamb.
Direct connection within the Passover celebration confirming the prohibition against leaving sacrificial meat until morning.
Complementary verses in the same chapter that together form the complete instruction for eating the Passover lamb.
